A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LENS research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original LENS evaluations on MTEB and AIR-Bench, architecture and cluster-count analyses, qualitative examples, and hybrid retrieval results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds distillation ablations, inference-time pruning results, and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds an evaluated inference variant that retains the K largest embedding activations and zeroes the rest without retraining. The clustered language-model head, bidirectional attention, pooling, and main training objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 56-dataset MTEB benchmark, English AIR-Bench 24.04 coverage, training mixture in Appendix A.2, and seven-dataset analysis subset in A.4. The added analyses introduce no distinct datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Gecko becomes an evaluated comparator in v2's pruning comparison, Table 6, at 768 and 256 dimensions; v1 only discussed it as related work. Comparator membership in the main MTEB, AIR-Bench, and hybrid retrieval comparisons is retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds contrastive-only training controls to the cluster-count study and evaluates inference-time pruning at 768, 512, and 256 active dimensions without retraining. The existing main-benchmark training budget, backbone, and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The analysis expands substantially: Figure 3 adds a distillation-loss ablation, Section 5.3 tests the sparsity–accuracy trade-off, and Section 5.5 provides four cases of semantically irrelevant cluster activations. The original cluster-count, attention/pooling, positive examples, and hybrid analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the LENS experiments. The added results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial pruning, distillation, and qualitative failure findings. Table 6 reports LENS-4000 BEIR averages of 60.01, 59.33, and 57.19 at 768, 512, and 256 active dimensions. Figure 3 adds contrastive-only results. Separately, Table 1 and the detailed appendix change LENS averages from 71.21/71.62 to 71.22/71.63 while retaining the per-dataset scores; these aggregate edits do not demonstrate new performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the mathematical formulation remain equivalent. The new pruning procedure and natural-sparsity discussion introduce no formal assumptions, theoretical results, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add the claim that LENS naturally supports inference-time dimension pruning without specialized Matryoshka training. The central claims about general-purpose lexicon-based embeddings, public-data MTEB performance, and hybrid BEIR performance remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains sparsification through distinct lexical-cluster dimensions and identifies subword overlap as a possible cause of semantically irrelevant activations. It proposes entity-level representations and frequency filtering as future remedies. The existing English-only, single-backbone, and computational-cost limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-model availability link on page 1 and newly specifies a 128-token query/passage limit for the reduced-data analyses. v1 supplied only the general 512-token setting. This additional analysis-specific disclosure does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references on Matryoshka learning, semantic residual embeddings, meta-task prompting, and sparse retrieval, while removing Formal et al. (2024). It also distinguishes PromptReps from fine-tuned Mistral-SPLADE and connects its new discussions to compression and entity-based retrieval research.

P1.justification: The abstract and several existing passages are refined, terminology and heading errors are corrected, and author affiliations and acknowledgements are updated. New analysis subsections extend the existing organization without substantially restructuring the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds pruning and failure-case tables, expands Figure 3 with a second curve and legend, and clarifies whitespace notation in qualitative displays. Existing hybrid and appendix tables are relocated or renumbered. The architecture diagram and overall two-column presentation are retained.

improvement.justification: The added distillation control, pruning measurements, and concrete failure cases improve scrutiny of LENS's design and limitations. Access information and the analysis-length disclosure also aid reproducibility. These are bounded gains over v1's extensive benchmark evidence: pruning's accuracy cost is documented, but runtime savings are not measured, and the main benchmark coverage and per-dataset results remain unchanged.
